text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The central bank opened bankrupcy proceedings for eight of the nine banks, placed in receivership on September 23 on the basis of insolvency.
-- The central bank cut its main interest rate to 15 percent monthly from 20 percent or 180 percent annually from 240 percent, in force from Monday. @
-- The central bank revoked the licences of 22 brokerage houses on the grounds of violating trading regulations.
-- Some $17 million of foreign investment are expected in Bulgarian resorts in 1997, a Tourist Committee official said.
-- The State Savings Bank (SSB), Bulgaria's largest saving institution posted 10.427 billion levs pre-tax profit for the first nine months of 1996, SSB director Bistra Dimitrova said. @

-- Agriculture Minister Krastyo Trendafilov has asked the central bank to extend around one billion levs for Bulgaria's agriculture, offering a seven milion Ecu collateral under a EU's PHARE programme credit line, Trendafilov told European Union's ambassador to Sofia Thomas O'Sullivan.

-- The licence of the Bulgarian private Mobiltel GSM operator will be transformed into a concesion and a tender for a concesion for a second GSM operator will be prepared, the Bulgarian Post and Telecommunication Committee decided. @
-- All Bulgarian livestock markets are closed down as a result of the foot-and-mouth desease outbreak in Southeast Bulgaria, the National veterinary service said.
-- Fifty nine Bulgarian companies have applied for investment intermediaries' licenses to the Securities and Stock exchanges commission.
-- Bulgaria's State Saving Banks (SSB) refinancing to local commercial banks rose by some 11 billion levs to 41.460 billion levs in the first nine months, SSB director said. @

-- A Mercedes car driven by Central Electoral Committee secretary and head of the liqudation team in Bulgarian Agricultural and Industrial bank exploded in central Sofia on Thursday but no one was hurt. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
